Housing census – Conventional dwellings – Time series from 2011 on,"The Housing census included in the Register-based census and in the Register-based labour market statistics is a complete survey of the buildings and dwellings and their attributes for the reference date 31 October. The Register-based census and the Register-based labour market statistics are conducted by using information from administrative registers. The main data source for the Housing census is the Buildings- and dwellings register of Statistics Austria. The characteristics and definitions are based on the EU regulation on population and housing censuses and the Austrian Register-based census act (BGBl. I. Nr. 33/2006). For a detailed description of the methods used and for further information see: https://www.statistik.at/en/statistics/population-and-society/housing/stock-of-buildings https://www.statistik.at/en/statistics/population-and-society/housing/stock-of-dwellings https://www.statistik.at/fileadmin/shared/QM/Standarddokumentationen/B_1/std_b_abgestimmte_erwerbsstatistik.pdf (German only) This database contains the results for all conventional dwellings. The dwelling stock in Vienna does not include apartments without residents, that were built between 2012 and 2023 as a result of extension, construction or conversion work. Conventional dwellings are structurally separate premises which are designed for permanent human habitation at a fixed location, with direct access from the street or from a public staircase. They consist of one room or suite of rooms as well as side rooms. The existence of a kitchen or kitchenette is not crucial. Rooms in hotels, student residencies and similar buildings are not counted as conventional dwellings. .) Territorial structure of 2024. .) Updating: annually last update: [2026-06-09] .) Urban-rural typology – Territorial structure of 2024,"Refers to the location of the building in which the dwelling is located, at the reference date 31 October of the respective year according to the urban-rural typology classification valid in 2024. Other Metadata: https://www.statistik.at/en/services/tools/services/regional-information/regional-divisions"
Occupancy status of the dwelling [partly ABO],"Classifies if there are persons, who are counted as part of the population at the reference date 31 October, usually resident in the dwelling."

One or more usual residents,"There is at least one person, who is counted as part of the population at the reference date 31 October, usually resident in the dwelling. In addition, the dwelling might also be used as a seasonal or secondary residence."

Only secondary residences,"There are no persons, who are counted as part of the population at the reference date 31 October, usually resident in the dwelling, but at least one person uses the dwelling as a seasonal or secondary residence."
No residents,"There are no persons, who are counted as part of the population at the reference date 31 October, usually resident in the dwelling, and there are no seasonal or secondary residences."
Useful floor space in square meters per occupant,"Describes the ""density standard"" of the dwellings referring to the average useful floor space per occupant."

Type of building (predominant use) [partly ABO],"Type of the building in which the dwelling is located. Classifies the buildings according to their predominant use. The categories are based on the EU-Classification of Types of Construction (CC)."
Buildings for institutional households,"Homes for the elderly, student residencies and similar institutions."
Buildings for public entertainment, education and health care,"Includes churches and other buildings for religious purposes."
Traffic and communication buildings,"Train stations, parking garages, telecommunication centres, radio and television broadcast buildings etc."
Office buildings,"Includes buildings for police and fire services."
Hotels and similar buildings,"Buildings for short-stay accommodation (hotels, motels, inns) or detached restaurants and bars."

Type of ownership,"Type of ownership of the building in which the dwelling is located. If the ownership of a building is divided between groups (co-ownership), the owner is defined as the one holding the highest share. If the shares are divided equally, the owner is defined as the one who is in charge of the decision making."
Other public bodies,"Chambers, national insurance institutions and recognized churches."

Limited profit housing associations,"Housing cooperatives and housing companies which have been assigned to be limited-profit associations according to the ""Limited-Profit Housing Act"" (profits are accepted but limited). Limited-profit housing associations also include housing companies which are partly owned by the federal state, the provinces or the municipalities."
Other enterprises,"Incorporated companies, limited liability companies, cooperatives which are not limited-profit associations, foreign housing companies, banks etc."
Other types of ownership,"Includes associations or foundations not covered by the other categories."
Period of construction [partly ABO],"Time period in which the building in which the dwelling is located has been finished."
